answer: A reputation bond makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock a stake that vests slowly over verified work, like water carving a karst cave grain by grain, so a single operator spinning up thousands of fake identities pays the full bond for each one. A lightweight zephyr of free activity is allowed, but earning trust requires sustained, checkable contributions, and slashing burns the stake of any identity caught colluding. The old fable of one wolf in many sheep skins fails here, because every skin costs real capital and time to grow.
